From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Mike / Connor — reviewed Acme's tracked changes. Summary and recommended positions below. I'm attaching a short response file with redline snippets (KP_proposed_responses.docx).

Key observations:
- Scope ambiguity: Acme's language ties indemnity to any "use of the Services" by Acme which is overly broad and would capture downstream model-invented outputs. Need to narrow to: (a) claims arising from Acme-provided Customer Data or Acme modifications to the service; or (b) claims tied to materials Acme controls.
- Model-output claims: Acme demands full defense for third-party claims alleging that model-generated content infringes. We should offer a compromise: defend-and-indemnify for claims directly caused by Acme's input material (training/prompts) or by explicit customer content; for 'model-only' allegations, propose a capped reimburse remedy or mutual cooperation with right of Redwood to assume defense if we choose.
- Notice & evidence: Acme's template requires extensive evidence within a 5-business-day window. Operationally, we can provide request logs, timestamped output snapshots, and user account IDs for the request. We cannot produce raw training datasets or internal model weights. Suggest we require notice + completion of evidence template to trigger Redwood's indemnity obligations.
- Insurance/escrow: suggest adding an insurance-first clause (exhaustion of available insurance before cash out) or an escrow/cap tied to order form value.

Proposed next steps:
1) Send Acme a consolidated legal response (short cover note + KP_proposed_responses.docx) that: narrows scope, proposes defend-vs-reimburse split, clarifies notice/evidence requirements, and asks for a reasonable damages cap tied to the order form value.
2) Connor/Mike to provide deal levers we'll use in negotiation (commitments, bundled services) so we can trade limited indemnity for commercial value.
3) Technical ask: we need a one-page evidence template listing the artifacts we can produce and the timelines for retention (logs kept for 90 days by default; we can set 365 days for enterprise with appropriate fees). I'll flag anything we can't produce.

I'll circulate redline snippets in the attached doc. If Acme pushes hard on defend-for-model-output, we should escalate to execs for approval on cap/insurance trade.

—Kimberly Park
Associate General Counsel, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

Laura — thanks for the redlines and the quick turn. Wanted to be explicit on the commercial/technical path we think will get us to a practical outcome. On Mon, Aug 30, 2026 at 11:05, Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com> wrote:
> Kimberly — looping you in to lead legal response / redline. High-level points I want us to evaluate...

Commercially: Acme is an important early customer; we're willing to make targeted concessions if we (a) narrow the indemnity trigger, (b) get a reasonable cap tied to annual committed spend, and (c) secure an enterprise retention/retention-fee for extended log retention. Specifics we propose to offer in negotiation: defend-for-customer-content; for model-output, a capped reimburse/remediation with Redwood option to assume defense.

Technical evidence we can provide (please confirm receipt and feasibility):
- Request logs (request_id, timestamp, endpoint, model-version) — retained 90 days by default, 365 days on enterprise terms.
- Output snapshot(s) — we can preserve a snapshot of the generated text and associated request metadata if a claim is raised (we'll need the request_id or approximate timestamp).
- Prompt bundle — if the claim is tied to a specific prompt or uploaded file, provide the file and the prompt text.
- Hashes & provenance markers — we can provide request hashes to help correlate outputs.
- No access to underlying training corpus or internal model weights; we can provide model provenance and third-party model license references where applicable.

Operational ask for triage: please complete the attached evidence template when you notify us (infringement_evidence_request_template.pdf). That will allow our team to pull logs and preserve snapshots immediately.

Scheduling: Can we do a short call to align legal + technical + commercial tomorrow (Aug 31) at 15:00 PT? We've created a short negotiation plan in the attached commercial_negotiation_plan.xlsx and linked the HubSpot deal here: https://hubspot.redwood.example/deals/ACME-2026-0914.

If that time doesn't work, propose alternatives.
